summary.name: ImageAlpha
summary.one_liner: ImageAlpha is a discontinued macOS app that losslessly-looking shrinks 24-bit PNG files, including alpha transparency, by converting them to lossy PNG8+alpha.
use_cases: Shrinking PNG images with transparency for websites
Reducing 24-bit PNG to PNG8 with alpha
Batch compressing PNGs from the command line
Comparing PNG compression quality on different backgrounds
Optimizing old web graphics for IE6-era browsers
summary.what_it_does: ImageAlpha is a macOS app that converts true-color PNG images into smaller PNG8+alpha files using lossy compression. You drag an image into the window and it converts automatically, with options for Median Cut or Posterizer compression and a Dithered mode. You can reduce the number of colors to shrink the file further. It lets you preview the result on different backgrounds, and it can make nearly opaque colors fully opaque for better IE6 display. It is based on pngquant, and a compiled pngquant binary is included in the app bundle for command-line batch processing.
notable: Lossy conversion of 24-bit PNG with alpha to PNG8+alpha
Based on pngquant with a bundled command-line pngquant binary
Preview on custom and palette backgrounds, with IE6-friendly alpha option
Free GPL v2 open-source software written in Python
caveats: No longer supported; written in Python 2, which has been removed from macOS
Page suggests alternatives: ImageOptim lossy option, pngquant, or squoosh.app
